svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 2. What end-to-end encryption covers, and what it leaves
svg.desc: A message split into two parts. The content is protected by end-to-end encryption. The surrounding record is not, and it names who spoke to whom, when, how often, from where, and on what. Two real subpoena outcomes are compared: Signal supplied two timestamps, while a document on WhatsApp described far richer metadata being available. The band below states that the difference between those two is a design decision, not an encryption strength difference, since both use the same underlying protocol for content.
svg.text: Figure 2: Two Platforms, Same Encryption, Different Answers
End-to-end encryption is a property of the content. What surrounds the content is a separate design decision.
"Critical injection flaw in the payment path.
Proof of concept attached. Roughly ten million
accounts exposed. Do not forward this."
The provider cannot read any of this.

g.text: Which two accounts, and at what exact moment
How large the message was, and whether a file came with it
How often you two speak, and who replies first
Which addresses each of you connected from
Which application, which version, which device
None of this is content, so none of it is encrypted content.

svg.text: What each provider actually handed over when compelled
Signal, responding to a grand jury subpoena

g.text: No contacts, no groups, no message records, because
the service was built not to hold them.

svg.text: WhatsApp, per a leaked law enforcement document

g.text: Under a pen register order, metadata on a target every
Under a warrant, the target's address book contacts, and
details of other users who hold the target in theirs.

svg.text: Both of those services encrypt content with the same underlying protocol.
So the difference between those two responses is not encryption strength. It is a choice about what to collect and keep. Lesson 1.1 made this point as
Myth 3 and it is the single most useful idea in this module: "is it end-to-end encrypted" and "what does it know about me" are two separate questions,
and a platform can answer the first one perfectly while answering the second one badly. Ask both, every time.
